newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers says Japan demand still soft.
newsitem.headline: De Beers says Japan demand still soft.

text.p: Diamond giant De Beers said on Tuesday that demand in Japan was unlikely to improve much in 1997 from its depressed levels in the second half of 1996.
The country's economic hard-times and depreciation of the yen have hit at demand for De Beers' luxury gems and there is only a slim chance of an upturn.

"(Japan) had strong first half sales but they gradually fell in line with imports during the year...there is a chance that Japan will improve towards the end of the year (1997), but we still feel that it will be very similar for most of the year," said Anthony Oppenheimer, president of De Beers' Central Selling Organisation (CSO).
Through the London-based CSO De Beers controls about 75 percent of the world's diamond trade.
Oppenheimer was speaking at a news conference to announce De Beers' year results. The firm posted a sparkling rise in earnings per share to 354 U.S. cents from 259 cents before.
Oppenheimer said that retail diamond demand had been disappointing in Japan and several other Asia-Pacific countries, such as Thailand.
However, in the United States demand had been good as an economic boom and high levels of consumer confidence had boosted sales.
Oppenheimer said 1997 should continue in the same vein. "Valentines Day has been extremely good and most retailers feel that 1997 might be a better year than 1996," he said.
In Europe the picture was more mixed with Britain seeing healthy demand, while France and Italy posted lesser gains. In Germany demand was poor.
